title: How Did a Fake Spy Fool Hitler in 1943? 🕵️
description:

pinned_comment: Which detail would have convinced you: the love letters, the theatre tickets, or the angry tailor's bill?
topic: Operation Mincemeat (1943: a fake officer's body with forged letters fooled Hitler into reinforcing Greece and Sardinia instead of Sicily)
script:
Britain's best spy of 1943 never said a word.
His papers said Major William Martin,
who never existed.
His pockets held love letters, theatre tickets,
and an angry tailor's bill.
A briefcase chained to his wrist held secret letters:
the Allies would hit Greece and Sardinia.
The body was really Glyndwr Michael, a homeless Welshman.
A submarine left him floating off Spain.
Spanish officers let German agents copy everything.
Hitler bought it and sent tanks to Greece.
The real target was Sicily.
The message to Churchill: Mincemeat swallowed rod, line and sinker.
So would a tailor's bill have fooled you?
key_facts: April 1943: HMS Seraph released a body off Huelva, Spain; a fisherman found it on 30 April
Fake identity: Major William Martin, Royal Marines; real man Glyndwr Michael, a homeless Welshman
Pocket litter: letters from his fiancée and father, theatre ticket stubs, tailor's bills complaining about late payment
Briefcase chained to the wrist held a letter implying attacks on Greece and Sardinia
Pro-German Spanish officers let German agents copy the letters
Hitler ordered Greece and Sardinia reinforced; the 1st Panzer Division moved from France to Greece
The Allies invaded Sicily in July 1943
Message to Churchill: 'Mincemeat swallowed rod, line and sinker'
